prompt: How do double-bond cleavage reactions differ from the alkene additions earlier in the chapter?

choices.text: They break the carbon skeleton, giving two carbonyl-containing fragments
They keep the carbon skeleton and turn the C=C into a C–C single bond
choices.why: That describes the earlier addition reactions.

choices.text: They add an −OH group to each carbon of the double bond
choices.why: That is hydroxylation, which keeps the carbon skeleton intact.

choices.text: They form a three-membered ring from the double bond
choices.why: Three-membered rings come from epoxidation; cleavage reagents split the molecule.

explanation: In the additions seen so far, the C=C bond becomes a single bond but the carbon skeleton is unchanged. Powerful oxidizing reagents such as ozone and KMnO4 cleave the C=C bond and give two carbonyl-containing fragments.

prompt: How is ozone, O3, prepared for ozonolysis?

choices.text: By passing oxygen through a high-voltage electrical discharge
By heating potassium permanganate, KMnO4, in acidic solution
choices.why: KMnO4 is a separate cleavage reagent; ozone is made from O2 in an electrical discharge.

choices.text: By treating hydrogen peroxide, H2O2, with aqueous base
choices.why: Basic H2O2 is the oxidant in hydroboration–oxidation, not a source of ozone.

choices.text: By reducing an ozonide with zinc metal in acetic acid
choices.why: Zinc reduction converts an ozonide into carbonyl compounds.

explanation: Ozone is prepared by passing a stream of oxygen through a high-voltage electrical discharge. It adds rapidly to C=C bonds at low temperature.

prompt: What happens first when ozone adds to a C=C bond at low temperature?

choices.text: A cyclic molozonide forms, which then rearranges to an ozonide
An ozonide forms, which then rearranges to a molozonide
choices.why: The order is reversed: the molozonide forms first and rearranges to the ozonide.

choices.text: Two carbonyl compounds form directly from the alkene
choices.why: The carbonyl compounds form only after the ozonide is reduced, for example with zinc.

choices.text: A cyclic osmate forms, which is then cleaved by NaHSO3
choices.why: Cyclic osmates come from OsO4, not ozone.

explanation: Ozone adds rapidly to a C=C bond at low temperature to give a cyclic molozonide. The molozonide spontaneously rearranges to an ozonide, coming apart into two fragments that recombine in a different way.

prompt: Why is the ozonide treated right away with a reducing agent such as zinc in acetic acid?

choices.text: Low-molecular-weight ozonides are explosive, so they're reduced rather than isolated
Zinc turns the ozonide back into the original alkene before it can decompose
choices.why: Reduction gives carbonyl compounds; the C=C bond has already been cleaved.

choices.text: Zinc oxidizes the ozonide further, to carboxylic acids and CO2
choices.why: Zinc is a reducing agent; carboxylic acids and CO2 come from KMnO4 cleavage.

choices.text: Ozonides are far too unreactive to break apart without help from zinc
choices.why: The issue is that low-molecular-weight ozonides are explosive.

explanation: Low-molecular-weight ozonides are explosive and are therefore not isolated. Instead, the ozonide is immediately treated with a reducing agent, such as zinc metal in acetic acid, to give carbonyl compounds.

prompt: What products form when an alkene with a trisubstituted double bond is ozonized and then reduced with zinc?

choices.text: One ketone and one aldehyde
Two ketones
choices.why: Two ketones come from a tetrasubstituted double bond.

choices.text: Two aldehydes
choices.why: The double-bond carbon with two substituents becomes a ketone.

choices.text: One carboxylic acid and CO2
choices.why: Carboxylic acids and CO2 come from KMnO4 cleavage, not ozonolysis with zinc reduction.

explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C bond and puts a doubly bonded oxygen on each original alkene carbon. A carbon with two R groups becomes a ketone, and one with an R and an H becomes an aldehyde. A tetrasubstituted alkene gives two ketones; a trisubstituted one gives one ketone and one aldehyde.

prompt: What products form when isopropylidenecyclohexane, in which a ring carbon of cyclohexane is double-bonded to a C(CH3)2 group, is treated with O3 and then Zn, H3O+?

choices.text: Cyclohexanone and acetone
Cyclohexanone and propanal
choices.why: The C(CH3)2 carbon carries two methyl groups, so it becomes a ketone, acetone, not an aldehyde.

choices.text: A single open-chain dicarbonyl compound
choices.why: The double bond is outside the ring, so cleavage gives two separate molecules.

choices.text: Cyclohexanol and 2-propanol
choices.why: Ozonolysis followed by zinc gives carbonyl compounds, not alcohols.

explanation: The double bond is tetrasubstituted, so two ketones form. The ring carbon becomes cyclohexanone, and the C(CH3)2 carbon becomes acetone.

prompt: When KMnO4 in neutral or acidic solution cleaves an alkene, what do double-bond carbons that carry hydrogens become?

choices.text: A carbon with one H becomes a carboxylic acid; a carbon with two H becomes CO2
A carbon with one H becomes an aldehyde; a carbon with two H becomes formaldehyde
choices.why: That's the pattern from ozonolysis with zinc reduction. KMnO4 gives carboxylic acids and CO2.

choices.text: A carbon with one H becomes a ketone; a carbon with two H becomes CO2
choices.why: A ketone carbon needs two carbon substituents; a carbon with one H becomes a carboxylic acid.

choices.text: A carbon with one H becomes CO2; a carbon with two H becomes a carboxylic acid
choices.why: This is reversed.

explanation: KMnO4 in neutral or acidic solution cleaves alkenes to carbonyl-containing products. If hydrogens are present on the double bond, carboxylic acids are produced; if two hydrogens are on one carbon, CO2 is formed.

prompt: 3,7-Dimethyl-1-octene, CH2=CHCH(CH3)CH2CH2CH2CH(CH3)2, is cleaved with KMnO4 in acid. How many carbon atoms does the carboxylic acid product contain?
explanation: The =CH2 carbon (carbon 1) becomes CO2, and carbon 2, which has one H, becomes a CO2H group. The acid keeps 9 of the alkene's 10 carbons: 2,6-dimethylheptanoic acid, formed in 45% yield.

prompt: What happens when a 1,2-diol whose two −OH groups are on a ring is treated with periodic acid, HIO4?

choices.text: The C–C bond between them breaks, giving one open-chain dicarbonyl compound
The C–C bond breaks, giving two separate carbonyl compounds
choices.why: That happens when the −OH groups are on an open chain. On a ring, the pieces stay joined.

choices.text: Water is removed and the diol is converted back into an alkene
choices.why: HIO4 cleaves the C–C bond; it doesn't remove water.

choices.text: An epoxide forms from the two neighboring −OH groups, with loss of water
choices.why: Epoxides come from peroxyacids or from halohydrins with base, not from HIO4.

explanation: Periodic acid cleaves 1,2-diols through a cyclic periodate intermediate. If the −OH groups are on an open chain, two carbonyl compounds result; if they are on a ring, a single open-chain dicarbonyl compound forms.

prompt: What alkene would give a mixture of cyclopentanone and propanal, CH3CH2CHO, on ozonolysis followed by zinc reduction?

choices.text: Propylidenecyclopentane, with a ring carbon double-bonded to CHCH2CH3
Ethylidenecyclopentane, with a ring carbon double-bonded to CHCH3
choices.why: That would give acetaldehyde, CH3CHO, rather than propanal.

choices.text: 1-Propylcyclopentene, with the double bond inside the ring
choices.why: Ozonolysis of a ring double bond gives a single open-chain dicarbonyl compound, not two molecules.

choices.text: 3-Hexene, CH3CH2CH=CHCH2CH3, a symmetrical open-chain alkene
choices.why: That gives two equivalents of propanal and no cyclopentanone.

explanation: Work backward: remove the oxygen from each product and join the two former carbonyl carbons with a double bond. The ring carbon of cyclopentanone becomes double-bonded to the CH carbon of propanal, giving a cyclopentane ring with an exocyclic =CHCH2CH3 group (Worked Example 8.8.1).

prompt: What is the product when 1-methylcyclohexene is treated with O3 and then Zn in acetic acid?

choices.text: CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CHO
CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CO2H
choices.why: That is the KMnO4 product. Ozonolysis with zinc reduction gives an aldehyde at the carbon that had one H.

choices.text: CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2COCH3
choices.why: Only the methyl-bearing carbon becomes a ketone; the other double-bond carbon had an H and becomes an aldehyde.

choices.text: Cyclohexanone and formaldehyde
choices.why: The double bond is in the ring, so cleavage opens the ring into one molecule.

explanation: Cleaving the ring C=C bond opens the ring into a single chain. The methyl-bearing carbon becomes a ketone (CH3CO–) and the carbon with one H becomes an aldehyde (–CHO): CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CHO.

prompt: What is the product when 1-methylcyclohexene is treated with aqueous acidic KMnO4?

choices.text: CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CO2H
CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CHO
choices.why: That is the ozonolysis and zinc product. KMnO4 turns a double-bond carbon with an H into a carboxylic acid.

choices.text: HO2CCH2CH2CH2CH2CO2H and CO2
choices.why: The methyl-bearing carbon has no H, so it becomes a ketone, and no carbon is lost.

choices.text: CH3CH(OH)CH2CH2CH2CH2CO2H
choices.why: KMnO4 gives carbonyl products; the methyl-bearing carbon becomes a ketone, not an alcohol.

explanation: KMnO4 cleaves the ring double bond. The methyl-bearing carbon, with no H, becomes a ketone; the carbon with one H becomes a carboxylic acid: CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CO2H.

prompt: Which alkene gives acetone, (CH3)2C=O, and formaldehyde, H2C=O, on ozonolysis followed by zinc?

choices.text: 2-Methylpropene, (CH3)2C=CH2
Propene, CH3CH=CH2
choices.why: Propene would give acetaldehyde and formaldehyde, not acetone.

choices.text: 2-Methyl-2-butene, (CH3)2C=CHCH3
choices.why: That would give acetone and acetaldehyde, CH3CHO.

choices.text: 2,3-Dimethyl-2-butene, (CH3)2C=C(CH3)2
choices.why: That would give two equivalents of acetone.

explanation: Remove the oxygens and join the two carbonyl carbons with a double bond: (CH3)2C= and =CH2 give (CH3)2C=CH2, 2-methylpropene.

prompt: Which alkene gives two equivalents of propanal, CH3CH2CH=O, on ozonolysis followed by zinc?

choices.text: 3-Hexene, CH3CH2CH=CHCH2CH3
1-Hexene, CH2=CHCH2CH2CH2CH3
choices.why: That would give formaldehyde and a five-carbon aldehyde.

choices.text: 2-Hexene, CH3CH=CHCH2CH2CH3
choices.why: That would give acetaldehyde and a four-carbon aldehyde.

choices.text: Cyclohexene
choices.why: A ring double bond gives a single open-chain dicarbonyl compound, not two molecules.

explanation: Joining two identical CH3CH2CH= fragments with a double bond gives CH3CH2CH=CHCH2CH3, 3-hexene.

prompt: When one molecule of cyclohexene is ozonized and the ozonide is reduced with zinc, how many separate organic product molecules form?
explanation: Both double-bond carbons are in the ring, so cleaving the C=C bond opens the ring rather than splitting the molecule in two. The result is a single open-chain compound with a carbonyl group at each end, just as 1-methylcyclohexene gives CH3COCH2CH2CH2CH2CHO.
